# Overall
 
SPI have 4 pins:
* mosi -> master output slave input 
* miso -> master input slave output
* clk -> clock line (generated by master)
* nss -> chip select signal (for single slave we put it as a low for transmission this is explained in another .md file (explaining_ssm_ssi_pins.md))

the way to program from scratch spi: 


check code in driver_development.
but it should go as follow:
1. Enable GPIO clock
2. configure gpio pins (set alternate mode for them -> see table for each pin with their alternate function) check gpio_driver.c. Check also alternate function mapping on data sheet for microcontroller
3. Set peripherial clock for correct SPI
4. Configure spi peripherial
If You want interrupts:
5. enable nvic interrupt for spi
6. enable spi peripherial


## Important note
if You want just receive bytes from slave device, master should send dummy bytes in order to generate clock cycles and through that slave is able to send data.![alt text](image.png)
